evidence.field: Summary; Source; Permission; Licensing; file history
evidence.text: The page identifies 牛-seal.svg as 牛 in a Shuowen seal-script style. It attributes the image to the Sinica Database and Chinese Etymology, and links to a specific Sinica image record (27.725B) and a Chinese Etymology image record (s00814). The page states the file is available under CC0 1.0 and lists file revisions dated 7–8 August 2009 and 14 June 2018. This is a modern vector illustration of a seal-style form, not an excavated specimen or evidence for the earliest form; it can illustrate a later graphic form but cannot independently confirm disputed interpretations of Shang forms.
evidence.title: File:牛-seal.svg

evidence.text: The page lists oracle-bone, bronze, Chu manuscript, small-seal, and Shuowen headings. It says the graph emphasizes the ox’s head and horns and originally referred to the animal. Its inspected text does not date individual specimens.

search_audit.query: Opened the supplied exact Commons leads 牛-seal.svg and Shuowen Seal Radical 019.svg, their image URLs, and the Academia Sinica 牛 form-evolution entry.
search_audit.outcome: The 牛-seal.svg page opened and supplied graph identification, source attributions, CC0 licensing, and revision dates. Its standalone SVG URL was rejected by the web tool as an unsupported image content type; the Commons page included a rendered preview. The second candidate page returned cache misses and its SVG URL was inaccessible. Academia Sinica’s form-evolution entry opened and supported the scoped distinction between a listed seal form and earlier form classes.

gaps: The second Commons candidate’s identity, source, and license remain unverified because its page returned cache misses; do not select it.
The verified seal image is a modern vector rendering, not a dated artifact. Neither it nor the paleographic entry establishes individual specimen dates or the earliest securely dated 牛 graph.
